evidence.quote: At today’s meeting, the Committee also decided to double the pace of reductions in its asset purchases.

There’s a real risk now, we believe, I believe, that inflation may be more persistent and that may be putting inflation expectations under pressure, and that the risk of higher inflation becoming entrenched has increased.
I don’t think that’s at all likely in this cycle. We’re in a very, very different place with high inflation, strong growth, a really strong economy.
Well, the labor market is, by so many measures, hotter than it ever ran in the last—in the last expansion, if you think about it.
It, it is a provision that would enable us to, in this case, because of high inflation, move before achieving maximum employment.
The rise in COVID cases in recent weeks, along with the emergence of the Omicron variant, pose[s] risks to the outlook.

parsed.rationale: The Chair announces a doubled taper pace, signals rate hikes soon after the taper ends with no long delay, and expresses forceful concern about persistent, entrenched inflation amid a very tight labor market. Omicron risks are noted but downplayed relative to inflation risks.
